newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to invest 11 billion pesos in electricity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to invest 11 billion pesos in electricity.

text.p: Mexico plans to invest 11 billion pesos ($1.4 billion) in electricity generation, distribution, maintenance and privatization studies in 1997, the director of the government's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) said late Monday.
"We have an investment with our own funds of approximately 11 billion pesos on a national level," CFE director Rogelio Gasca Neri told reporters.
He added that the CFE is auctioning $2 billion in projects, including electrical energy generation plants in Baja California and Yucatan states, and possibly in Jalisco.
The results of the auction of the Yucatan generator called Merida III will be given before Feb. 7 and is scheduled to begin operations in 1999, Gasca said.
In Baja California, the CFE plans to auction a 250 megawatt plant for private operation planned to begin production in 2000.

For the geothermic plant southeast of Jalisco's largest city, Guadalajara, Gasca said the CFE is waiting for ecological authorization to begin studying privatization for the 50 megawatt, $70 million plant.
About 95 percent of Mexicans have access to electrical energy, and the country has 570 generation units, Gasca said.
